March Filing Fee Retention

How much did the courthouse retain from filing fees collected in March, rounded to the nearest dollar?

The problem

In March the courthouse processed:

  • 420 civil filings at $85 each
  • 175 family-law filings at $120 each
  • 60 probate filings at $210 each

Rules:

  • A 6% state surcharge is added to every filing fee.
  • Electronic filers get a $5 credit per filing. 70% of civil, 40% of family-law, and 25% of probate filings were electronic.
  • The courthouse retains 82% of the collected total; 18% goes to the state.
  • The $9,400 from the passport-services desk is separate and is not part of filing fee collections.

Step 1: Base fees

Case typeFilingsFeeBase total
Civil420$85$35,700
Family law175$120$21,000
Probate60$210$12,600
Total base fees655$69,300

Step 2: Add the 6% state surcharge

$69,300 × 1.06 = $73,458

Step 3: Electronic filing credits

Case typeElectronic shareElectronic filings
Civil70% of 420294
Family law40% of 17570
Probate25% of 6015
Total electronic filings379

Credits: 379 × $5 = $1,895

Step 4: Total collected

$73,458 − $1,895 = $71,563

The $9,400 in passport revenue is excluded; it is not a filing fee.

Step 5: Courthouse share (82%)

$71,563 × 0.82 = $58,681.66

Rounded to the nearest dollar: $58,682. (The remaining $12,881.34 is remitted to the state.)

Final answer

$58,682

The courthouse retained $58,682 from March filing fees.
